category: Health and Fitness (iOS, US App Store)
method: Apple public search (fetch_reviews.py search) and public customer-review RSS feed (fetch_reviews.py reviews, 3 pages per app, saved rating<=3 reviews only). Raw review text saved under state/scout/reviews/<app id>.json. No WebFetch pages used. No Reddit. No keyword-volume source was available to the scout.
excluded_note: Nothing researched matched data/excluded_categories.yaml. Nothing in Health and Fitness was on state/scout/rejected.jsonl (those entries cover Productivity, Business and Education only). Price-only and paywall-only complaint clusters (free-trial charges, 'not free', subscription price) were seen at large volume on Strong, Stronger, Fitbod, HitMeal, Calo, Liftoff and Yazio and were deliberately not made candidates.

injection_suspected.text_quoted_as_data: Alternative: turn to LLM, tell it the gym equipment you’re using. Tell LLM the weights, the reps, and any other details necessary to log your workout.
injection_suspected.note: Low confidence. Reads as a reviewer addressing other readers, not an instruction aimed at an agent. Not followed and not used as a recommendation.

injection_suspected.text_quoted_as_data: Fitbod has gotten so bad go to gravl
injection_suspected.note: Low confidence. Imperative aimed at readers, competitor steering. Not followed. Gravl was not researched.

coverage_notes: Reviews were read for 13 apps in total. Hevy returned only 5 reviews at 3 stars or under across 3 pages, so it is thin. Runmeter's feed pages contain many reviews dated 2018 to 2023; only items dated 2026 are used as recent evidence below.
The feed only returns most-recent reviews, 3 pages per app. Counts below are therefore a sample, not a measure of how common each problem is across all users.

Several Strong, Hevy and Fitbod reviews dated 2026-10-27 to 2026-11-14 ask for iPhone Duo layout support (for example https://itunes.apple.com/us/rss/customerreviews/page=1/id=464254577/sortBy=mostRecent/json, 2026-11-08). This is an update-lag complaint rather than a capability gap and is recorded only as a note.

Candidates c1, c3 and c8 touch related ground (Apple Watch, data safety and integrations). They are listed separately because the complaint clusters differ, but the caller should treat the core-job overlap as an open question.
Several Yazio reviews are in Russian. They were read but are not quoted here, since the quotes would not be usable as English verbatim evidence.
No keyword volume or difficulty source was available. No WebFetch or web search was run, so there are no external trend sources.

candidates.not_found: Apple Fitness was not read. Hevy sample is small (5 low-rated reviews). Complaints are concentrated on Strong, so breadth across apps is moderate. No evidence on how many users run workouts from the watch alone.

trend_signals.signal: Reviewers on Nike Run Club say they run Strava alongside it to cross-check or replace it, and one says Nike layoffs may mean the app is not maintained.

candidates.not_found: Runmeter has only one 2026 complaint on distance recording (title only, no text). Its older complaints from 2018 to 2023 are not used. adidas Running and Polar Beat were not read, so only two apps carry the evidence. The two large apps are free, so no evidence on willingness to pay for a replacement. No GPS accuracy measurements were gathered by the scout.

No evidence on whether users would pay for a backup or import tool as a standalone product. Not checked: whether competing apps already offer export or import and how well they work, apart from one Strong reviewer who describes a CSV export buried in settings (https://itunes.apple.com/us/rss/customerreviews/page=2/id=464254577/sortBy=mostRecent/json, 2026-07-03).

trend_signals.signal: Several Fitbod reviewers say a recent update or an AI coach beta made their plans worse, and two name other apps they are moving to.
One Fitbod reviewer says a general-purpose LLM can replace the app for workout logging and planning.

candidates.not_found: Caution on claims: the Fitbod reviewer on 2026-10-13 links the problem to injury risk. Health-claim territory was avoided, and this entry reports only the planning behaviour. Fitbod complaints are about 5 of the 11 above, so evidence is weighted to one app. Hevy was not mined for this job.

trend_signals.signal: A cluster of Yazio reviews between 2026-07-23 and 2026-07-29 object to a Quick Add change that replaced manual entry with AI estimation. At least 6 separate reviews in that window; 4 are quoted or cited above.

candidates.not_found: Yazio's developer reply (quoted in a 2026-07-29 review) says AI is optional with a toggle, and the reviewer disputes this; the scout cannot verify the app state. The nutrient-tracking part is evidenced mostly on HitMeal. Calorie Counter + and Appediet were not read. Most tracker reviews in this sample are about ads, price or free-trial billing, which are excluded from this candidate. Diet and nutrient reviews carry health-claim risk and were kept to logging behaviour only.

candidates.not_found: This is the most crowded sub-area in the sample: the store search for calorie counters returned at least 10 competing apps, and most carry AI scanning. The scout did not test any scanner and found no accuracy benchmark. Whether a differentiated capability exists here is not established by this evidence.

candidates.not_found: Evidence is spread across many apps but each complaint is a single integration (Strava, Apple Health, Garmin, Coros, scale apps), so there is no single clear target. Strava, Apple Health and Garmin themselves were not researched, and they may be the competitors for this job. Apple platform capability limits were not checked. Overlaps with c1 and c3.
